description:
A top-level `require` (or `import`) of a module defined earlier in the same file gives a misleading error:

    defmodule M do
      def f(), do: 7
    end
    require M
    dbg(M.f())

fz: "resolve/unknown-function: function `main/0` is not defined" (also with an explicit def main instead of statements; pre-dates script mode). Elixir refuses the program too, clearly: "module M is not loaded but was defined. This happens when you depend on a module in the same context in which it is defined."

Decide (paper first): support it, as fz publishes all definitions before main runs, or refuse it with a clear diagnostic naming the require and the module. Either way the error must not be about main/0. A fixture of a remote expression macro at the top level (the script-mode decision of 2026-10-23) arrives with this. Not needed by the distiller.
title: A top-level require of a same-file module is not reported as a missing main/0
